finding: Partial proof, not the asserted trace-norm convergence of the projected finite-rank kernels. The passage lifts quotient biorthogonals to the orthogonal complement of the completed half-twisted theta isotype and says the lifted finite-rank kernels still converge in trace norm, in the context of a fixed norm-one isotype, positive symmetric width, supported smooth test and degree zero. With the accepted Hilbert quotient projection Q and complement inclusion S, the new operator S B Q is operator-norm isometric, carries each quotient Riesz rank-one term to the actual ambient rank-one term with both vectors included, and transports arbitrary finite cutoffs. If a quotient remainder is given with summable norm products and pointwise synthesis, the corresponding ambient rank-one series has summable operator norms and synthesizes the lifted remainder in operator norm. An ordinary-import client applies these facts to the actual half-twisted rational radial trivial-isotype quotient, full represented theta range and bounded intertwiner (accepted f3c1b67400b3d180a586a682ceec1a8b140f9f1480d372e489b4f455be29f4da receipt) at positive width and s=0: the row is ell composed with quotient convolution and Q, and the operator limit when the hypotheses hold is projection after ambient convolution, as in (10.4.2.5), not the reverse order printed in (10.4.3.45). Output projection cannot supply the missing transpose on bare rows. No analytic trace norm, absolute-ordinate spectral estimate, weighted kernel convergence, or diagonal is proved. The p. 472–473 projective convergence assertion assumes s>1 and does not discharge the degree-zero claim.
retry: For the actual degree-zero expansion, identify bounded full interior jets annihilating the global theta closure with the specified original quotient biorthogonals and check the pairings; prove trace-norm Cauchy control of the full transpose-regularized absolute-height blocks and identify their limit with the descended convolution. For the checked operator-series bridge, give summable norm products and pointwise synthesis for the actual rank-one remainder, not just decay of spectral coefficients. For a full Lean trace-norm transport, supply the infinite-dimensional trace ideal (or a proved equivalent norm) and prove zero-extension preserves its norm. Treat any representative/diagonal claim separately.
